originalTitle: Market wrap: Top gainers and losers on Nifty and Sensex today
simplifiedContent: The Indian stock market had a bad day on Tuesday, with the two main indexes (Sensex and Nifty) falling in value. The Sensex dropped by 238 points and the Nifty ended below 24,200. Some big companies like HDFC Bank, Reliance Industries, and SBI did poorly, which hurt the overall market. However, smaller companies did better, with some indexes that track them actually going up. This mix of good and bad news shows that the market is a bit unpredictable, even when there are worries about what's happening in the world.

originalTitle: Indian rupee gains as oil comes off; inflows, RBI intervention in focus
simplifiedContent: The Indian rupee, the country's currency, went up a bit on Tuesday. This happened because there's a chance that the US and Iran might have better relations, which could reduce tension in the oil market and lead to lower oil prices. The Indian central bank, called the Reserve Bank of India, also got a lot of money coming into the country, over $20 billion, which helped the rupee. This is important because it means the country has more money in its foreign exchange reserves. Investors are now watching to see how the central bank will manage these reserves.

originalTitle: Eternal Q1 Results Preview: All eyes on Blinkit to drive earnings. Here's what investors can expect
simplifiedContent: Eternal is about to release its financial results for the first quarter, and investors are focusing on how well its subsidiary Blinkit performed. Blinkit is expected to have done well due to opening more stores and having customers place larger orders. Investors want to see if Blinkit can make a profit from its quick delivery service and if it can maintain its growth in a competitive market. They will also be listening to what the company's management has to say about how it plans to keep growing. This information is important because it will help investors understand how well Eternal is doing and make decisions about their investments.

originalTitle: US stock market today: S&P 500, Nasdaq futures rise up to 1.4% as chip stocks rebound after last week's rout
simplifiedContent: Here's what's happening in the US stock market: the S&P 500 and Nasdaq futures are going up, with some stocks rising as much as 1.4%. This is because technology stocks, especially those related to computer chips, are bouncing back after a recent decline. The increase in stock prices is happening despite some concerns about oil prices and global energy security due to rising tensions in West Asia. This matters because it shows that investors are still optimistic about the market, even with some potential risks on the horizon. The upcoming earnings reports from big tech companies will also be closely watched to see how they affect the market.

originalTitle: SBI has no plans for further stake sale in SBI Funds after IPO: chairman Setty
simplifiedContent: SBI Funds Management, a company that manages investments, recently had an Initial Public Offering (IPO), which means it sold shares to the public for the first time. The company's shares started trading on the stock market at ₹613.30, which is 6.85% higher than the IPO price of ₹574 per share. The chairman of SBI, Setty, said that SBI does not plan to sell any more of its ownership in SBI Funds Management. This means that SBI is committed to holding onto its stake in the company. The successful listing and higher-than-expected share price suggest a positive start for SBI Funds Management as a publicly traded company.

originalTitle: Lohia Corp IPO: 10 key things investors should know before subscribing to  ₹1,101.28 crore public issue; check GMP
simplifiedContent: Lohia Corp, a company that makes machinery for technical textiles, is raising money by selling shares to the public, called an IPO, for ₹1,101.28 crore. This means they are asking people to invest in their company. The company made ₹17,169.95 million in revenue last year, which is a measure of how much money they earned. The shares are expected to start trading on the stock exchanges NSE and BSE on July 30, 2026. Investors can subscribe to buy shares in July, and it's essential for them to know these details before deciding to invest.
